deferred_source_units.reason: The ordinary Davidic end-heading does not identify a particular event or provide a distinctive independent relationship.
The request to hear a prayer and deliver from an enemy's fear does not identify the enemy or establish a more particular link than general rescue prayer.
The text says God will be exalted and their blows became an infants' arrow. It is not rewritten as God shooting an arrow, and no secure independent counterpart for the actual image is retained.

The heading names David, Jeremiah and Ezekiel and refers to an account of sojourning when they were about to depart. Its composition, attribution, departure and the pronoun's referents are not resolved by importing a standard psalm heading or assumed exile event.
The signs at earth's ends and rejoicing departures of morning and evening are preserved without assigning the departures to a specific cosmic or travel event.

The text says rams are clothed and valleys abound with grain and sing. It is not silently rewritten as pastures clothed with flocks, and the whole image has no sufficiently precise retained counterpart.
The trap and afflictions upon the back are not assigned to Egyptian slavery or another named captivity from these images alone.

The supplied line joins crying with the mouth to lifted up beneath my tongue. Its unusual final phrase is not made passive or replaced with a familiar praise-on-the-tongue wording to manufacture a link.
God's listening and attending to the petition is preserved; a general assertion of answered prayer does not provide a sufficiently particular additional counterpart.
The final blessing for prayer and mercy not rejected is not linked solely by the common themes of divine mercy and hearing.
The end-heading, Among hymns and psalm-of-song designation do not establish a distinctive separate relation or particular historical occasion.
The general end-heading, psalm and song labels for David do not establish a particular episode or sufficiently distinctive separate relation.
The living creatures dwelling there and preparation for the poor are preserved without identifying the creatures or supplying an unstated object such as bread to force a more specific comparison.
The wording about the king of powers, the beloved and beauty of the house dividing spoil does not establish the identity of a king, victor or battle.
The allotted portions and dove with silvered wings and gold-green back are not assigned to a named people, trophy or historical incident.
Selmon and snow after the heavenly One distinguishes kings do not establish the proposed identification with Abimelech's wood-cutting mountain. The named-place candidate remains uncredited.
The rich and curdled mountain is preserved without replacing it with an unexpressed mountain name or deciding which physical mountain the description denotes.
Daily blessing and the God of salvations do not furnish a specific independent connection beyond a broad praise-and-salvation formula.
The Lord says I will return from Bashan and I will return in the depths of the sea. The line is not rewritten as bringing enemies back, and the identity or occasion of this return is unresolved.
The divine King's processions in the holy place do not establish the particular ark procession in Chronicles. That historical identification remains a zero-credit candidate.
Benjamin, Judah, Zebulun and Naphtali are named in this gathering, but no particular historical tribal assembly is identified by these names alone.
The petition that God command His power and strengthen what He accomplished for the community does not identify a particular act or army.
Giving glory to God, His magnificence upon Israel and His power in clouds are not combined into a retained match on the strength of a general glory command alone.
Attending to the soul and redeeming because of enemies is not assigned an independent target merely from common redemption-and-enemy language.
God's knowledge of reproach, shame and the people afflicting the speaker who are before Him remains this lament; it does not identify a separate trial scene or a particular historical group.
The request to add lawlessness to lawlessness and bar entry into divine righteousness is not flattened into an ordinary forgiveness or judgment formula.
Poverty, pain and the declaration that the salvation of God's presence supported the speaker have no retained independent link more particular than a general suffering-and-rescue theme.
Magnifying and praising God's name in song is preserved without retaining a generic praise verse solely because it shares that activity.
Hope in the Lord from youth is not assigned a separate counterpart on the basis of lifelong trust alone; the more concrete womb language in the following unit has its own retained comparison.
Being a portent to many and having God's strong help do not identify the particular sign-children in Isaiah or another named portent.
A mouth filled with praise throughout the day is not given a separate target through a general continual-praise theme alone.
Continued hope and addition to praise remain this speaker's resolve without an independently established specific relationship.

The proposed Isaiah comparison does not contain the expected righteousness-and-strength formula in this pinned text. The psalm's entry in God's power and remembrance of His righteousness alone remain pending rather than supported by an outside-edition wording.

Teaching from youth and the present announcement of wonders are not given a separate counterpart from general instruction and praise language; the following explicit future-generation purpose has a distinct retained comparison.
Mountains taking up peace and hills righteousness are not identified with named rulers or transformed into an ordinary agricultural blessing.

The ruler descending like rain upon a fleece and drops upon earth is preserved. Gideon's fleece involves dew and an explicit two-part sign, while the proposed Davidic rain passage has different supplied wording; neither specific allusion is established.
Sparing the poor and saving the needy's souls is retained as the royal portrait, without an additional target supported only by general mercy toward the poor.
